title: Module Header: Closing the Equivalence Chain
content: The file imports three parents: Mathlib.Tactic (core tactics), Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2 (the Euclidean space model for R^n), and the two preceding files in the Brouwer chain: BrouwerFixedPoint.lean (providing the geometric ray construction and classical BFP structure) and BrouwerFixedPointOQ01OQ02.lean (providing the singular homology no-retraction theorem). The docstring lays out the complete three-step equivalence chain: singular_homology_retraction_split → no_retraction_singular_homology (in OQ01OQ02.lean) → brouwer_fixed_point_via_singular_homology (this file). The axiom accounting is careful: 0 new axioms are introduced here — the total count of 2 axioms is the same as in BrouwerFixedPoint.lean, but the opaque no_retraction_axiom is replaced by the more explanatory singular_homology_retraction_split.
mathContext: The file works in the namespace `BrouwerOQ01OQ02OQ03` with `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` as the model of $\mathbb{R}^n$. The closed ball $B^n = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : \|x\| \leq 1\}$ is `Metric.closedBall (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1` and the sphere $S^{n-1} = \{x : \|x\| = 1\}$ is `Metric.sphere 0 1`.

title: Namespace and Linter Setup: Suppressing an Intentional Unused Variable
content: `set_option linter.unusedVariables false` is required because `no_retraction_from_bfp` (Part III) has a BFP hypothesis `(_ : ∀ f : Brouwer.SelfMap n, Brouwer.HasFixedPoint n f)` that is deliberately unused — the no-retraction conclusion follows directly from singular homology axioms without invoking BFP. The linter would flag this as a warning without the suppression. The namespace `BrouwerOQ01OQ02OQ03` scopes all five theorems in this file. `open Metric Set` brings `closedBall`, `sphere`, and set-builder notation into scope, matching the conventions of the parent files.
mathContext: In Lean 4, `set_option linter.unusedVariables false` suppresses diagnostics for bound variables appearing in a type but not in the proof term. The pattern `fun (_ : P) => proof_not_using_P` is logically sound but the linter warns. This is intentional here: the theorem has the correct logical type (BFP → no-retraction) but the proof is a direct shortcut via the stronger singular homology result.

title: Retraction Type Conversion: Definitional Equality Bridge
content: The key technical lemma is `toSingularRetraction`: a function converting a `Brouwer.Retraction n` (from BrouwerFixedPoint.lean) to a `BrouwerOQ01OQ02.Retraction n` (from BrouwerFixedPointOQ01OQ02.lean). Both structure types have four identical fields: `toFun`, `continuous'`, `maps_to_sphere`, and `fixes_sphere`. The field types are definitionally equal across namespaces because `Brouwer.ClosedBall n` and `BrouwerOQ01OQ02.ClosedBall n` both unfold to `Metric.closedBall (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1`, and similarly for `UnitSphere`. In Lean 4, definitional equality is checked by the kernel (not the elaborator), so no explicit coercion tactic is needed — just copy the fields directly. The companion theorem `toSingularRetraction_toFun` (line 94) confirms the underlying function is preserved: the proof is literally `rfl`, because the underlying function is literally the same object (not just propositionally equal). This is definitional equality being used as a proof engineering tool: the two independently developed API layers happen to reduce to the same types, allowing field-copy construction with zero proof overhead.
mathContext: Lean 4's kernel equality: two types $A$ and $B$ are definitionally equal if they reduce to the same normal form. Here, $\text{Brouwer.ClosedBall}(n) = \text{Metric.closedBall}(0, 1) = \text{BrouwerOQ01OQ02.ClosedBall}(n)$. This means any term of type $\text{Brouwer.Retraction}(n)$ is automatically accepted where type $\text{BrouwerOQ01OQ02.Retraction}(n)$ is expected at the field level. The `rfl` proof of `toSingularRetraction_toFun` holds because `.toFun = r.toFun` is definitionally true — no rewriting needed.

title: BFP via Singular Homology: The 4-Step Contradiction
content:
The main theorem `brouwer_fixed_point_via_singular_homology` is a 4-line proof by contradiction:
1. `by_contra h` — assume f has no fixed point.
2. `let r_brouwer := Brouwer.retraction_construction f h` — the geometric ray construction: if f(x) ≠ x for all x ∈ B^n, draw a ray from f(x) through x, extending to the boundary S^{n-1}. This gives a continuous retraction r: B^n → S^{n-1} of type `Brouwer.Retraction n`. The geometric argument requires solving ‖f(x) + t·(x-f(x))‖² = 1 for t > 0 — a quadratic equation whose positive root varies continuously with x.
3. `let r_sh := toSingularRetraction r_brouwer` — convert to `BrouwerOQ01OQ02.Retraction n`.
4. `exact BrouwerOQ01OQ02.no_retraction_singular_homology n hn ⟨r_sh, trivial⟩` — the homological contradiction: a retraction r∘i = id on S^{n-1} forces H_{n-1}(r) ∘ H_{n-1}(i) = id on H_{n-1}(S^{n-1}) ≅ ℤ, but H_{n-1}(B^n) = 0 makes any such factorization through the trivial group impossible.
mathContext: The contradiction is: a retraction $r: B^n \to S^{n-1}$ with $r \circ i = \mathrm{id}$ (where $i: S^{n-1} \hookrightarrow B^n$ is inclusion) would give $H_{n-1}(r) \circ H_{n-1}(i) = \mathrm{id}$ on $H_{n-1}(S^{n-1}) \cong \mathbb{Z}$. But $H_{n-1}(B^n) = 0$ (the ball is contractible), so $H_{n-1}(i) = 0$, making $H_{n-1}(r) \circ 0 = \mathrm{id}$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ — absurd since $0 \neq \mathrm{id}$ as maps $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$.

title: The Complete Equivalence: No-Retraction ↔ BFP
content:
Part III establishes the full logical equivalence between the two formulations of BFP. Three theorems:

1. `no_retraction_from_bfp`: nominally BFP → No-Retraction, but note that the BFP hypothesis `(_ : ∀ f : Brouwer.SelfMap n, Brouwer.HasFixedPoint n f)` is entirely UNUSED in the proof — the proof is just `BrouwerOQ01OQ02.no_retraction_singular_homology n hn` directly. This is why `set_option linter.unusedVariables false` appears at the top of the file. The no-retraction result is independently available from singular homology axioms, so the BFP assumption is vacuous. This is an intentional design choice: the theorem has the right logical type, but the proof is a shortcut.

2. `singular_homology_implies_bfp`: a named alias for `brouwer_fixed_point_via_singular_homology`, making the full logical chain `singular homology axiom → BFP` explicit and directly referenceable.

3. `no_retraction_axiom_iff_sh`: both no-retraction propositions are equivalent. Forward direction: convert Brouwer.Retraction to BrouwerOQ01OQ02.Retraction via inline structure literal (the same definitional equality used by `toSingularRetraction`, but inlined); backward: use `toSingularRetraction`. This establishes that the two `Retraction` types are interchangeable for the no-retraction statement.
mathContext:
The equivalence $
eg\exists r: 	ext{Brouwer.Retraction}(n) \leftrightarrow 
eg\exists r: 	ext{BrouwerOQ01OQ02.Retraction}(n)$ holds because the two types have the same definitional structure. In classical topology: no-retraction ↔ BFP is the standard equivalence. The ray construction provides no-retraction → BFP; a retraction $r: B^n 	o S^{n-1}$ would give $r \circ (\mathrm{include} \circ r): B^n 	o B^n$ as a fixed-point-free map (its value $r(r(x))$ lies on $S^{n-1}$ hence $
eq r(x)$ generically), giving BFP → no-retraction.
